rows.recommendation: One typed parser (strict integer >= 0, fail loud) used by riskManager, preflight and both dashboard routes; count open positions by exit lifecycle (AUD-DB-003). Card OD-25 (defaults and parser), DB-01 (what counts).
rows.name: Maximum open positions (all chains together)
rows.comparison: canSnipe: count of status='pending' buys >= max -> refuse (riskManager.ts:111-120); preflight wallet floor multiplies the snipe amount by it (preflight.ts:200-202)
rows.representation: riskManager and risk.ts parseInt(x || "10"); preflight Number() + Number.isInteger; chains.ts raw string
rows.effective_empty: 10 at all four sites (|| in riskManager/routes; preflight treats '' as unset)
rows.effective_non_numeric: riskManager NaN (count >= NaN false, would never refuse) but preflight returns passed:false and boot exits FATAL, so the running bot never sees it; '7.9' -> riskManager 7, preflight refuses; '0' -> refuses every snipe (floor = gas buffer only)
rows.overlap: TH-BUY-27 (BUY consumer row); the per-chain wallet floor TH-DB-18 multiplies by this global count on every chain; counts only status pending, so failed-held positions are not counted (AUD-DB-003). Size mismatch on the OD-25 risk defaults: MAX_TOTAL_EXPOSURE 10.0 is 1000 x the ETH snipe (0.01), 100 x the deployment the default position count allows (10 x 0.01 = 0.1 ETH) and about 800 x the ~0.0124 ETH funded wallet named in config.ts:136-139, so the exposure cap cannot bind at the defaults; the position count and the wallet balance are the real limits.

rows.recommendation: Fix the unit and accounting basis first (card DB-01), then decide a cap that can bind (for example a multiple of the snipe size or of the funded wallet, per currency) on card OD-25; validate at boot.
rows.name: Maximum total exposure (all chains together)
rows.comparison: canSnipe: getTotalExposure + snipe amount > cap -> refuse (riskManager.ts:139-148); getTotalExposure sums amount_in of status='pending' buys minus partial-sell proceeds (db.ts:425-438)
rows.units: 'native currency' per the description, but ETH and BNB amounts are summed into one number, and the stored proceeds are wei (AUD-DB-002)
rows.representation: float (parseFloat of the env string; CAST AS REAL in SQL); amounts are not compared in wei
rows.effective_non_numeric: NaN: total + amount > NaN is false, the cap never refuses (fail-open); '5ETH' -> 5 (prefix accepted)
rows.overlap: TH-BUY-27; Size mismatch on the OD-25 risk defaults: MAX_TOTAL_EXPOSURE 10.0 is 1000 x the ETH snipe (0.01), 100 x the deployment the default position count allows (10 x 0.01 = 0.1 ETH) and about 800 x the ~0.0124 ETH funded wallet named in config.ts:136-139, so the exposure cap cannot bind at the defaults; the position count and the wallet balance are the real limits. After one partial sell the stored total is about -proceeds-in-wei and the check is always false (AUD-DB-002).

rows.recommendation: Validate at boot (positive decimal or unset) and compare in wei. Card OD-25.
rows.name: Maximum position size per snipe
rows.comparison: canSnipe: maxPositionSize !== null && parseFloat(snipeAmount) > maxPositionSize -> refuse
rows.representation: float; truthiness check on the raw string (not ||)
rows.effective_unset: null: no cap (documented: use the chain snipe amount)
rows.effective_non_numeric: NaN: amount > NaN is false, the cap the operator set does nothing (fail-open); '0' refuses every snipe
rows.overlap: TH-BUY-27; the deliberate buy path never calls canSnipe (by design, AUD-BUY-010 sibling note), so the cap does not apply there

rows.recommendation: Fix the loss accounting (card DB-01) before choosing a value; validate at boot (card OD-25).
rows.name: Daily loss limit (percent of per-chain max capital, rolling 24 h)
rows.comparison: canSnipe: getDailyRealizedLoss(chain, now - 86400) <= -(maxCapital * pct / 100) -> refuse for that chain
rows.representation: float (parseFloat); the loss sum is a REAL in SQL over mixed decimal and wei strings
rows.effective_non_numeric: NaN: threshold NaN, the breaker never trips (fail-open); '0' -> threshold -0 and 0 <= -0 is true, every snipe refused; negative refuses every snipe
rows.overlap: TH-BUY-27; base is TH-DB-07; the breaker does not count ordinary losing trades because of the unit mix-up (AUD-DB-002) and charges each partial sell the full cost (AUD-DB-013); the dashboard computes daily loss differently (api/routes/risk.ts:66, :91-95)

rows.recommendation: Validate at boot (card OD-25); reserving the cooldown at canSnipe time is card BUY-03.
rows.name: Snipe cooldown per chain
rows.comparison: canSnipe: Date.now() - lastSnipeTime[chain] < cooldown -> refuse; lastSnipeTime set by recordSnipe after a buy was submitted (bot.ts:1125, :1449, :772)
rows.effective_non_numeric: NaN: Date.now() - last < NaN is false, no cooldown (fail-open); '0' no cooldown; '30s' -> 30 ms
rows.rationale: D-09 (in-memory, ephemeral by design) in the comment at riskManager.ts:38-40
rows.overlap: TH-BUY-27; the map is empty after every restart; recorded only after the submit returns, so concurrent handlers all pass (AUD-BUY-010)

rows.recommendation: Validate as a positive decimal with <= 18 decimals at registry load (fail loud like chainRegistry.ts:701-714) and store amounts in wei (card DB-01). Card OD-25 for the values.
rows.name: Per-chain snipe amount
rows.comparison: no comparison at the definition; buy value (parseEther), canSnipe size/exposure input (parseFloat), wallet floor multiplicand, entry floor term, stored as the buy row amount_in
rows.representation: string; bigint wei via parseEther for the buy and floors; float in canSnipe; stored as the decimal string (AUD-DB-002)
rows.effective_non_numeric: preflight parseEther throws inside its try -> passed:false -> boot FATAL (fail-closed); '0' accepted (no positive check)
rows.overlap: TH-BUY-01 (BUY consumer row), TH-EXIT-24 (price probe); the legacy CONFIG.snipeAmountETH 0.01 duplicates the ETH value (config.ts:280, TH-DB-23). Size mismatch on the OD-25 risk defaults: MAX_TOTAL_EXPOSURE 10.0 is 1000 x the ETH snipe (0.01), 100 x the deployment the default position count allows (10 x 0.01 = 0.1 ETH) and about 800 x the ~0.0124 ETH funded wallet named in config.ts:136-139, so the exposure cap cannot bind at the defaults; the position count and the wallet balance are the real limits.

rows.recommendation: Decide whether it is a cap (enforce per-chain deployed <= maxCapital) or a loss base (rename) on card DB-01; validate at boot (OD-25).

rows.effective_non_numeric: NaN -> daily-loss breaker disabled for the chain (fail-open); no boot validation anywhere
rows.rationale: none stated; documented as "Max ETH deployment" (.env.example:16) which the code does not do
rows.overlap: TH-BUY-28 (BUY consumer row); TH-DB-04

rows.recommendation: Require a finite value with an upper bound and treat future blocks beyond a small skew as a failure (card DB-04); decide whether the defaults should follow the stated 5x rule (card OD-25).
rows.name: Per-chain RPC block-age tolerance (preflight)
rows.current_value: ETH 300 s, BSC 60 s, Base 30 s, Arbitrum 30 s
rows.comparison: boot: now - latest block timestamp <= tolerance -> pass
rows.representation: Number() of the env string; rejected when NaN or <= 0
rows.effective_non_numeric: log.fatal + exit (explicit rejection, fail-closed); 'Infinity' and huge values accepted (check can never fail); a block dated in the future always passes
rows.rationale: '~5x chain block-time' (config.ts:144-146, chainRegistry.ts:163-165), which no value matches: ETH 300 s = 25 blocks, BSC 60 s = 20 blocks, Base 30 s = 15 blocks, Arbitrum 30 s = about 120 blocks
rows.overlap: checked only at boot; no mid-run staleness check in this slice

rows.recommendation: Make the first signal wait (up to the grace) for in-flight buys and their row before closing the DB. Card OD-18.

rows.recommendation: Keep the value; note it in the 22-13 lock design (one bot per file) and keep script writes short.

rows.effective_non_numeric: n/a

rows.recommendation: Decide synchronous=FULL on card OD-18 (research: negligible cost).
rows.name: SQLite durability mode
rows.current_value: journal_mode = WAL, synchronous = NORMAL (pause/resume add wal_checkpoint(FULL))
rows.comparison: WAL frames are written on commit and fsynced only at checkpoints
rows.effective_non_numeric: n/a
